issues.t: Rear fuel tank can leak after a rear crash (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing in normal driving. The risk shows up after a rear-end collision, when fuel can leak from the tank behind the rear axle.
issues.why: The fuel tank sits low at the very back of the vehicle, where a hard hit from behind can damage it. A recall added a factory-designed tow hitch to help shield it.
issues.next: Look up your VIN for recall 13V-252 and have the inspection and hitch work done. If you smell fuel after any rear impact, do not drive it; have it towed.

issues.t: Rear liftgate sticks closed
issues.sym: The rear hatch will not open from the handle or opens only after several tries.
issues.why: The liftgate latch and its linkage wear and bind with age, and rust along the bottom of the hatch can make it worse.
issues.next: Have the latch and linkage cleaned, lubricated or replaced. Check the bottom edge of the hatch for rust while you are at it.

issues.t: Factory alarm acting up
issues.sym: The security alarm goes off for no reason, will not arm or disarm properly, or the remote stops working reliably.
issues.why: The original alarm system on this generation is known to become unreliable as it ages.
issues.next: Have the alarm module and door switches checked. A shop can repair or bypass a failed factory alarm.

issues.t: Violent front-end shake (death wobble)
issues.sym: After hitting a bump, usually somewhere around 35 to 50 mph, the front end and steering wheel shake violently and keep shaking until you slow way down.
issues.why: These models use a solid front axle. Worn or loose track bar mounts, steering joints or bushings let the axle start oscillating side to side.
issues.next: Slow down gently until it stops and do not keep driving at speed. Have the track bar, its bolts and the steering parts inspected and fixed before regular use.

issues.t: Clicking behind the dash and wrong air temperature
issues.sym: A repeated clicking or tapping behind the dashboard, air that will not change temperature or vent, or hot air on one side and cold on the other.
issues.why: The small doors inside the heater box, and the motors that move them, wear out and break, so the system cannot route air where you ask.
issues.next: Have the blend or mode door actuator diagnosed and replaced. It is not a safety concern but will not fix itself.

issues.t: Power window drops or stops working
issues.sym: A window grinds, moves slowly, stops working, or falls down into the door and will not stay up.
issues.why: The window regulator and motor inside the door wear out and break on this generation.
issues.next: Have the window regulator and motor replaced. Tape or brace a dropped window to keep weather and thieves out until it is fixed.

issues.t: Airbags may go off without a crash (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Some owners see an airbag light. The front airbags, side curtains or seatbelt tensioners can fire while driving.
issues.why: A part inside the airbag control module can fail. The recall added a jumper harness to the module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 12V-527 (and any follow-up campaign) and have it done as soon as possible. Get an airbag warning light checked right away.

issues.t: Front seat heater can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A seat that gets too hot, a burning smell, or scorch marks on the seat cover.
issues.why: The electric heating element in the front seat can overheat. A recall was issued.
issues.next: Stop using the seat heater and check your VIN for recall 09V-117. Have it repaired before using the heater again.

issues.t: No-crank from wireless control module
issues.sym: The engine will not crank or start at random, and the keyless remote may stop working. It may work again after the battery is disconnected, then come back.
issues.why: The wireless control module that handles the key and remote can lock up electronically and block starting.
issues.next: Have the module tested before replacing the starter or battery. A dealer or shop can reset or replace it.

issues.t: A/C water can get into the transmission (recall)
issues.sym: A shudder as the transmission locks up at cruising speed, signs of overheating, or smoke and fluid around the engine bay.
issues.why: Condensation from the A/C can drip into the transmission fill tube seal. The water boils and can push transmission fluid out onto hot parts, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 05V-396. If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, pull over, shut it off and have it towed.

issues.t: Transfer case can slip into neutral (recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle loses drive power, or rolls when parked without the parking brake set, because the transfer case went to neutral on its own.
issues.why: An electrical fault in the transfer case controller can shift it into neutral. The recall updated the controller software.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V-175 and get the update. Always set the parking brake until it is done.

issues.t: Knee can bump the key and shut off the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off while driving, along with power steering and power brakes, often after a knee touches the key or key ring.
issues.why: The ignition switch can be knocked out of the run position. Airbags may not deploy when that happens. The recall replaced the ignition switch.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V-438. Until it is done, keep only the vehicle key on the ring and adjust the seat so your knee clears the key.

issues.t: Brake pedal can disconnect from booster (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels loose or goes to the floor with little braking.
issues.why: A retaining clip that holds the brake booster input rod to the pedal may be missing or not seated. The brakes can fail without warning.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 10V-009. If the pedal feels wrong, do not drive; have it towed.

issues.t: Rear track bar problem (recall)
issues.sym: The rear of the vehicle feels loose or unstable, especially in turns or over bumps, and you may hear clunking.
issues.why: The rear track bar keeps the rear axle centered under the body. A defect in it can reduce stability. A recall was issued.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 10V-085. Have the rear suspension inspected before highway driving if it feels unstable.

issues.t: Key can come out before shifting to Park (recall)
issues.sym: You are able to remove the key while the shifter is not in Park, and the vehicle can roll after you walk away.
issues.why: A fault in the wireless ignition node allows the key to be removed out of Park. A recall was issued.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 10V-200. Always confirm Park and set the parking brake before leaving the vehicle.

issues.t: Stalling or no-start from fuel pump relay (recall)
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, or stalls while driving. The horn, wipers or other electrical items may act up, or the fuel pump keeps running.
issues.why: The fuel pump relay inside the main fuse and relay module (TIPM) can fail. Earlier repairs were followed by a later recall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-813 (and earlier 14V-530 or 15V-115) and have the repair done.

issues.t: Left cylinder head wear on the 3.6L V6
issues.sym: Check engine light with a misfire (often cylinder 2), a ticking from the driver side of the engine, and rough idle.
issues.why: Valve seats and guides in the left cylinder head on early engines wear too fast. Chrysler extended warranty coverage on that head and released a revised part.
issues.next: Get misfire codes read promptly. Ask a dealer whether the left head extension applies to your engine.

issues.t: Oil filter/oil cooler housing leak on the 3.6L V6
issues.sym: A burning oil smell, oil at the back of the engine or on the transmission, a slowly dropping oil level, or coolant loss with no obvious leak.
issues.why: The plastic housing that holds the oil filter and oil cooler sits in the valley of the engine, where heat can crack it or harden its seals.
issues.next: Have it checked as soon as you smell burning oil. Keep oil and coolant topped up until the housing is replaced.

issues.t: Ticking from worn rocker arms on the 3.6L V6
issues.sym: A fast tapping or ticking from the top of the engine, sometimes with a rough idle and a misfire code.
issues.why: Rocker arms (cam followers) can wear or fail, and later revised parts have not fully ended the problem.
issues.next: Have a misfire or new ticking checked early. Running it long can damage the camshaft.

issues.t: Alternator failure can cause stalling (recall)
issues.sym: A battery or charging warning light, dim lights, electrical glitches, loss of steering assist, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: The alternator can fail suddenly. On some vehicles a failure can also short internally, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check recall status by VIN. Do not ignore a charging light; the vehicle may stall once the battery runs down.

issues.t: Confusing shifter can lead to rollaway (recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle rolls after you thought you put it in Park. The shift lever returns to center, so it is hard to tell the gear by feel.
issues.why: The electronic shifter's design made it easy to leave the vehicle in the wrong gear. A recall added software that shifts to Park when the door opens.
issues.next: Confirm recall 16V-240 is done, always check the gear display, and set the parking brake.

issues.t: Diesel EGR cooler cracking (recall)
issues.sym: Coolant level drops with no visible leak, white smoke or a coolant smell from the exhaust, or loss of power.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation cooler can crack and let coolant into the intake, where it can burn. A safety recall covers this because of a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-699. Do not keep topping off coolant without having the cause found.

issues.t: Diesel high-pressure fuel pump failure (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, stalling, or the engine will not restart.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pump can wear internally and send metal debris through the fuel system, starving the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-406. If power drops suddenly, get safely off the road and have it towed.

issues.t: Fuel rail crossover tube may leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell from under the hood or wet spots of fuel around the engine.
issues.why: On some Saltillo-built engines the tube that links the two fuel rails could be damaged during assembly and leak.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-814. Do not drive if you smell fuel under the hood; have it towed.

issues.t: EGR valve can stick open (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a check engine light, or a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation valve can stick open on a small number of engines. A recall was issued.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-284. If power drops, get safely off the road and have it checked before driving further.

issues.t: Rear coil spring can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from the rear over bumps, or the rear sitting unevenly. 2021 applies to the three-row Grand Cherokee L.
issues.why: The rear coil springs may not be seated correctly and can work loose while driving. Several recalls have been issued.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 23V-413, 26V-051 and 26V-562. If the rear clunks or sags, have it inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Front upper ball joint can separate (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front suspension, the steering pulling to one side, or uneven tire wear. 2021 applies to the Grand Cherokee L.
issues.why: The upper control arm ball joint can pull apart from the steering knuckle, letting the wheel tip outward.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-132. Have any front clunk or pull inspected right away.

issues.t: 4xe high-voltage battery fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning at all. Some vehicles show hybrid system warnings or lose drive power.
issues.why: The high-voltage battery can fail internally and catch fire, parked or driving. An earlier fix was replaced by a newer recall remedy.
issues.next: Look up your VIN for recall 25V-741 (which replaces 24V-720). Until repaired, follow recall instructions, which have included not charging and parking outdoors.

issues.t: 4xe engine debris can cause failure (recall)
issues.sym: Engine knocking or rough running, a check engine light, or reduced power.
issues.why: Debris left inside the engine during manufacture can damage it, leading to engine failure, loss of drive power or an engine-bay fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-766. Stop driving and have it towed if the engine starts knocking.

issues.t: Electronic throttle control light and sudden loss of power
issues.sym: The lightning-bolt electronic throttle control light and often the check engine light come on, the engine drops to idle or barely responds to the pedal, and it may stall at a stop.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body and the pedal and throttle position sensors wear and send readings the computer does not trust, so it cuts power to protect the engine.
issues.next: Get it diagnosed right away and avoid highway driving, since power can drop without warning. The repair is usually a new throttle body and a software update.
